title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
description:
# Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal

The arrays `preorder` and `inorder` record traversals of the same binary tree, whose node values are all distinct. Reconstruct the tree and return its root.

A traversal visits every node once and records its value:

* Preorder: visit the root, then the entire left subtree, then the entire right subtree.
* Inorder: visit the entire left subtree, then the root, then the entire right subtree.

Apply the same rule within each subtree. For a root `2` with left child `1` and right child `3`, preorder is `[2,1,3]` and inorder is `[1,2,3]`.

Example trees use a level-order display: list the root, then each existing node's left and right children in node order. `null` means an absent child; trailing nulls may be omitted. A tree node stores `val`, `left`, and `right`; tree parameters or return values in code are `TreeNode` objects.

## Example 1:

**Input:** preorder = [3,9,20,15,7], inorder = [9,3,15,20,7]
**Output:** [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]

## Example 2:

**Input:** preorder = [-1], inorder = [-1]
**Output:** [-1]

## Constraints:

* `1 <= preorder.length <= 3000`
* `inorder.length == preorder.length`
* `-3000 <= preorder[i], inorder[i] <= 3000`
* `preorder` and `inorder` consist of **unique** values.
* Each value of `inorder` also appears in `preorder`.
* `preorder` is guaranteed to be the preorder traversal of the tree.
* `inorder` is guaranteed to be the inorder traversal of the tree.

solutions.name: Recursive HashMap with Preorder Pointer
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a map from node value to its index in `inorder`. Then walk `preorder` with one shared pointer: the next preorder value is always the root of the current subtree, and its inorder index splits the current range into left and right subtrees.

## Key Insight

Preorder chooses roots, while inorder gives subtree sizes. The HashMap removes repeated scans, so each value is looked up and turned into a `TreeNode` once.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Recursive Explicit Index Boundaries
solutions.description:
## Approach

Pass explicit preorder and inorder ranges into each recursive call. The first value in the preorder range is the root, and a linear scan inside the inorder range finds where the left subtree ends and the right subtree begins.

## Key Insight

This slower baseline makes the range arithmetic visible: `leftSize` determines exactly how the preorder range must be split after the root.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(h)

solutions.name: Iterative Stack Reconstruction
solutions.description:
## Approach

Create nodes in preorder order and keep a stack of ancestors whose right child may still need to be attached. An inorder pointer tells us when the current left chain is complete and when the next preorder value must become a right child.

## Key Insight

If the stack top is not the current inorder value, the next preorder node is the top's left child. Otherwise, pop completed ancestors until the next node belongs as a right child.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h)

solutions.name: Recursive Inorder Stop Sentinel
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use preorder and inorder pointers without a map. A recursive call receives a stop value: when the current inorder value equals that stop, the current subtree is finished. The current preorder value still creates the root.

## Key Insight

The stop sentinel replaces explicit index ranges. The left subtree stops at the root value; after consuming the root in inorder, the right subtree stops at the parent's stop value.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h)
